body.p: A lazy girl. There lived a girl with her mother. The girl was lazy. The mother would say: "Ayoga, bring some water!" Ayoga would say: "I'll fall into the water." The mother: "Hold on to the bush!" She: "I will scratch my hands." Once her mother said: "Knead dough!" Ayoga said to this: "I will get my hands dirty." The mother kneaded the douigh herself. Then the mother said:[ShA:] The form nÉxiluta- is put, as such a verb exists.[ShA:] KÉleÅa is an unexpected form. "Ayoga, bake the bread!" The girl said to this: "I'll burn my hands!" The mother: "Put a mitten on!" The girl: "The mitten will burn." The mother baked the bread herself. She sat down to drink tea but did not call her daughter. The girl cried: "Why didn't you call me?" The girl cried out, she ran to the shore. There she saw her face in the water and said: "My face is nice." Suddenly she fell down into the water. She became a goose. She cries: "Ayoga, ga, ga, ga!"
